summary: You proposed a well-motivated single-satellite GBR fluid-lensing mission with plausible SSO and STK access analysis. Your introduction and structure are strong, but launch rationale and orbital mechanics contain errors and quantitative support is limited. Focus on correcting mechanics, adding calculations, and synthesising conclusions with proper referencing.
next_steps: Correct your SSO launch and RAAN reasoning in Mission Design and add sensor, delta-V, link and deorbit sizing calculations with STK files.
Strengthen your Conclusion to synthesise quantitative outcomes from your evidence rather than repeating the design.
Fix referencing and professional style in Bibliography and throughout by completing reference [10] and replacing non-approved sources.

criteria.C1: You did well in your Executive Summary and Introduction to define coral reef monitoring, justify need with bleaching statistics, explain why only one satellite is required, and identify CSIRO/BOM users with literature refs. To reach top of Accomplished, clarify vague funding detail.
criteria.C2: You covered launch from Guiana Space Centre, 600km 97.7924° SSO in Image 1, manoeuvres, and ground access well with STK views. To reach Accomplished, fix equatorial benefit for retrograde SSO, RAAN 27.33 deg and Argument of Latitude errors, and add FOV, delta-V, link and drag-sail decay estimates.
criteria.C3: You summarised launch, polar SSO illumination, ground station and Vega C alternative in your Conclusion. To reach Accomplished, move beyond repetition to detailed conclusions drawn from your evidence with specific quantitative outcomes and residual risks.
criteria.C4: You used clear headings, executive summary, and labelled STK plots/tables in Images 1 and 4. To reach Accomplished, ensure consistent formatting, formal language, matching in-text and list references, complete all entries, and use only approved sources.
